facts.fact: The Adwave guide on Google Business Profile posts is dated March 2, 2026.
The guide presents 9 industry-specific Google Business Profile post types.
facts.quote: We'll move beyond generic advice to give you 9 actionable, industry-specific post types, complete with templates, optimal timing, and expert insights.

facts.fact: Adwave recommends posting the 'Wednesday Wisdom' educational post on Wednesdays at 10 AM.
facts.quote: Wednesday Wisdom: Quick Tips for Creating Broadcast-Ready Ads (Post on Wednesdays, 10 AM)

facts.fact: Adwave recommends posting the 'Friday Feature' industry campaign ideas on Fridays at 2 PM.
facts.quote: Friday Feature: Industry-Specific Campaign Ideas (Post on Fridays, 2 PM)

facts.fact: Adwave recommends posting the 'Tuesday Trend Alert' premium channel and audience insights post on Tuesdays at 11 AM.
facts.quote: Tuesday Trend Alert: Premium Channel Placements & Audience Insights (Post on Tuesdays, 11 AM)

facts.fact: Adwave states that TV advertising through its platform offers an estimated CPM of $15-$35.
facts.quote: TV advertising through a platform like Adwave offers an estimated CPM of just $15-$35, making it an accessible and intelligent growth tool.

facts.fact: The page's example post headline contrasts a traditional TV ad costing $50,000+ with Adwave starting at $30 a day.
facts.quote: Traditional TV Ad: $50,000+ vs. Adwave: Starting at $30 a day.

facts.fact: The page's implementation guide states that Adwave campaigns start at $50.
facts.quote: campaigns starting at $50, no production crew needed

facts.fact: The page gives the example headline 'Why a $500/Month TV Budget Works for Local Businesses with Adwave', citing a $500 per month TV budget.
facts.quote: Why a $500/Month TV Budget Works for Local Businesses with Adwave

facts.fact: The page recommends posting the 'Budget Reality Check' content on Thursdays at 3 PM.
The page recommends posting the 'Data-Driven Friday' performance content on Fridays at 1 PM.
The page suggests structuring a Google Business Profile campaign challenge as a 30-day challenge.
facts.quote: A 30-day challenge creates a sense of community, urgency, and guided progress.

facts.fact: The page advises starting proactive holiday and event campaign planning at least 60 days before the event.
facts.quote: Proactive campaign planning, starting at least 60 days out, allows you to build momentum and align your offerings

facts.fact: The page recommends mapping out a 12-month calendar of key industry dates to plan Google Business Profile post themes.
facts.quote: Create a 12-Month Calendar: Map out key dates for your industry.

facts.fact: The page's pro tip refers to a set of 'big six holidays' as the major holidays to plan posts around, and advises looking beyond them to smaller events.
facts.quote: Don't just focus on the big six holidays.

facts.fact: The page suggests a weekly GBP posting rhythm with success stories on Monday, quick tips on Wednesday, and feature posts on Friday.
facts.quote: Monday's success stories build credibility, Wednesday's quick tips establish your authority, and Friday's feature posts provide direct value.
